thread:
kai: heads-up — proposal to switch from hard rejects to an adaptive queue + conditional degrade on region saturation. want to keep more requests alive for PLG customers without blowing p99s too much. thoughts?

maria: curious what "adaptive" means here — dynamic queue depth per-pool based on recent token burn?

kai: yep. basic idea: maintain target utilization window (e.g., 70-85%). when a pool exceeds upper bound, increase queue depth for non-rt routes, start best-effort degrade (lower max output tokens / lower sampling temp) for long-running jobs. only reject when queue + degrade > safety cap.

ahmed: example numbers? how do we avoid long tail enqueue time? p95/p99 matters for a lot of endpoints.

kai: initial numbers I tested on staging (30m synthetic load): p50 latency similar, p95 +40ms, p99 +180ms for queued requests vs baseline rejects. success rate for requests increased from 82% -> 96%. cost delta ~+2% token overhead due to replays.

sophia: +1 on higher success rate. customers hate spikes in 5xx. But we need per-customer SLAs enforced. Is quota calc affected?

kai: quotas still charged on execution only; queued time isn't billed. We will track queued_time and queued_attempts in the tracing. quota burn won't increase unless request executes.

ops-oncall: big concern: if network blips cause backlog, queue growth could cause memory pressure on router nodes. Need hard cap and an eviction policy.

kai: agreed. plan: per-node soft queue target derived from free memory and GPU queue length, hard cap absolute (config) e.g. 2000 requests/node. eviction order: oldest idle -> degrade -> reject.

maria: can we encode policy as simple config? sample: 
```json
{
  "admit_policy": "adaptive",
  "metrics_window_s": 60,
  "util_target": [0.7, 0.85],
  "soft_queue_per_node": "auto",
  "hard_queue_per_node": 2000,
  "degrade_rules": [{"route_regex":"/embed/.*","max_tokens":128},{"route_regex":"/chat/.*","sampler_temp":0.6}]
}
```

ahmed: testing strategy? canary? telemetry? we need clear KPIs (success rate, p99 latency, memory pressure, error rate).

kai: rollout plan: 0% -> 5% (1 region) -> 20% (multi-region) -> 100%. At each step we validate KPIs: success_rate >= baseline - 0.5%? and p99 latency increase <= 250ms for critical routes. If either fails we rollback.

sophia: add per-customer fairness: heavier customers get lower queue priority when pool stressed. We already have token-rate scores; can plug that in.

ops-oncall: add automated alert when queued_time_avg > 500ms + memory_free < 20% to flip to emergency reject mode.

kai: good. also plan to surface metrics in console: queued_count, queue_time_p50/p95/p99, degrade_rate, reject_rate, memory_free, gpu_util.

sophia: one more: cost ops — draining queued requests may increase GPU churn. ops, estimate cost delta at scale?

ops-oncall: rough estimate: if we convert 10% rejects into queued+executed, infra cost up ~3-6% depending on model mix. but customer LTV might offset that.

maria: ok. action items: 1) kai to open RFC with config schema + rollout gating 2) eng-infra to add eviction + memory safety checks 3) telemetry: add queued_time, degrade_rate, per-customer priority metrics 4) prod canary next Tue 9am PT if RFC approved.

kai: thanks. I'll draft RFC and attach sim logs. cc @ops-oncall @sophia @ahmed

deploy-bot: scheduled canary job created for 1899994321-adaptive-queue — run id: canary-189999. monitoring hooks: queue_metrics, degrade_events, reject_events.

ops-oncall: noted — I'll block that slot on oncall schedule and prepare rollback runbook.

kai: awesome — closing thread for now, will link RFC here when ready.
